LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_ONE.titleEnglish: Move the Thing into the Spotlight
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_ONE.learnerPromise: You can put the food, drink, gift, or thing you are talking about first.
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_ONE.explanation: Chinese can move a known thing to the front of the sentence. Pause, then say what the person does with it or how they feel about it. With several things up front, 都 means "all of them".

teachingGlossary.meaning: marks a new or strong situation
links a description or owner to a noun
how about it; okay or not
ending word that makes a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

discoveryLab.title: Move the spotlight, keep the meaning
discoveryLab.description: The thing at the start tells the listener what this sentence is about. What follows is what you think or do about it.

choices.label: One thing
choices.pinyin: Dàngāo, wǒ xǐhuān.
choices.note: 蛋糕 is in the spotlight. 我喜歡 says what you think about it.

choices.label: Several things
choices.pinyin: Shū, bǐ, wǒ dōu yǒu.
choices.english: Books and pens, I have both.
choices.note: Two things come first, so 都 means "both".

choices.label: Contrast two things
choices.traditional: 茶，我喜歡；咖啡，我不喜歡。
choices.simplified: 茶，我喜欢；咖啡，我不喜欢。
choices.pinyin: Chá, wǒ xǐhuān; kāfēi, wǒ bù xǐhuān.
choices.english: Tea, I like; coffee, I do not.
choices.note: Putting each drink at the start makes the contrast easy to hear.

choices.label: Repair the pause
choices.traditional: 我蛋糕喜歡 → 蛋糕，我喜歡
choices.simplified: 我蛋糕喜欢 → 蛋糕，我喜欢
choices.pinyin: Wǒ dàngāo xǐhuān → dàngāo, wǒ xǐhuān
choices.note: If you move a thing to the start, put it before the person and hear a small pause.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Put the thing first, pause, then say what you think or do.

patternRows.english: Books and pens, I have both.
The big and small ones, I want both.

items.question: When the thing goes first, do I need a pause?
items.answer: Yes — say the thing, pause, then the person and their feeling. In writing, that pause is a comma.

items.question: One thing up front — can I use 都?
items.answer: No. 都 means "all", so it needs two or more things. With one thing, just say 我喜歡.

items.question: I do not like coffee or tea. Where does 不 go?
items.answer: After 都: 都不喜歡. 都 + 不 means you feel this way about none of them.

right.english: Tea and coffee, I do not like either.

text.traditional: 茶，我喜歡；咖啡，我不喜歡。
text.simplified: 茶，我喜欢；咖啡，我不喜欢。
text.pinyin: Chá, wǒ xǐhuān; kāfēi, wǒ bù xǐhuān.
text.english: Tea, I like; coffee, I do not like.

text.traditional: 這枝鉛筆，我要；那枝鉛筆，我不要。
text.simplified: 这枝铅笔，我要；那枝铅笔，我不要。
text.pinyin: Zhè zhī qiānbǐ, wǒ yào; nà zhī qiānbǐ, wǒ bú yào.
text.english: This pencil, I want; that pencil, I do not want.

text.traditional: A：你要哪個禮物？ B：大的、小的，我都要。
text.simplified: A：你要哪个礼物？ B：大的、小的，我都要。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ yào nǎ ge lǐwù? B: Dà de, xiǎo de, wǒ dōu yào.
text.english: A: Which gift do you want? B: The big and small ones, I want both.

questions.correctFeedback: 紅色的衣服 comes first; 我喜歡 says what you think of it.

segments.hint: Spotlight this kind of pencil.

tiles.meaning: I do not want to buy it

questions.correctFeedback: The thing from the question comes first: 這種鉛筆，我要買.
questions.repairFeedback: Keep the thing first, and say who does what after it.

segments.traditional: A：你喜歡吃什麼東西？ B：

segments.hint: Name two foods before the pause.
Use 都 because you like both.

questions.correctFeedback: Two foods come first, so 都 means "both".
questions.repairFeedback: List both foods first. Add 都 before the shared action.

segments.traditional: A：你喜歡什麼生日禮物？ B：
segments.simplified: A：你喜欢什么生日礼物？ B：

segments.hint: List the gifts first.
All three share one opinion.

questions.correctFeedback: Three gifts come first; 都 means "all three".
questions.repairFeedback: When you feel the same about several things, use 都.

LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_THREE.lessonTitleEnglish: Would You Like Coffee or Tea?
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_THREE.learnerPromise: React naturally when something feels extremely hot, big, tiring, good, or delicious.
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_THREE.explanation: Wrap a description with 太 before it and 了 after it. The frame can mean “too,” or an enthusiastic “so” or “really,” depending on context.

teachingGlossary.meaning: marks a new or strong situation
links a description or owner to a noun
how about it; okay or not
ending word that makes a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

discoveryLab.title: Turn up the reaction meter
discoveryLab.description: 太…了 frames one description. Context tells you whether the reaction is delighted or uncomfortable.
discoveryLab.prompt: What kind of reaction do you hear?

choices.label: Delighted
choices.pinyin: Tài hǎo le!
choices.note: With 好, the strong reaction is enthusiastic and positive.

choices.label: Too much
choices.pinyin: Tài dà le!
choices.note: With 大, it can mean "too big" — more than what fits.

choices.label: Very impressed
choices.pinyin: Tài hǎochī le!
choices.note: With 好吃, the speaker reacts with delight.

choices.label: Close the frame
choices.pinyin: tài rè → tài rè le
choices.note: In this pattern, 了 closes the strong reaction.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Open with 太, name the feeling, close with 了.

complement.meaning: marks a new or strong situation
marks a new or strong situation
marks a new or strong situation

items.question: Can I just say 太熱?
items.answer: As a full reaction, no — close the frame with 了: 太熱了. 太 and 了 work as a pair.

words.meaning: marks a new or strong situation

items.question: Where does 太 go?
items.answer: Right before the describing word: 太累. The order is 太 + describing word + 了.

words.meaning: marks a new or strong situation

items.question: The shirt is much too big. Is 太好了 okay?
items.answer: No — 太好 sounds happy. Pick the describing word that fits: 太大了.

right.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài dà le.
right.english: This item of clothing is too big.

words.meaning: marks a new or strong situation

text.traditional: A：今天天氣怎麼樣？ B：今天太熱了。
text.simplified: A：今天天气怎么样？ B：今天太热了。
text.pinyin: A: Jīntiān tiānqì zěnmeyàng? B: Jīntiān tài rè le.
text.english: A: How is the weather today? B: It is too hot today.

words.meaning: how is it; what do you think
marks a new or strong situation

text.traditional: A：你今天好嗎？ B：我今天太累了，現在很想睡覺。
text.simplified: A：你今天好吗？ B：我今天太累了，现在很想睡觉。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ jīntiān hǎo ma? B: Wǒ jīntiān tài lèi le, xiànzài hěn xiǎng shuìjiào.
text.english: A: How are you today? B: I am too tired today; I really want to sleep now.

words.meaning: marks a new or strong situation

text.traditional: A：那家餐廳的牛肉麵怎麼樣？ B：太好吃了，我常常去吃。
text.simplified: A：那家餐厅的牛肉面怎么样？ B：太好吃了，我常常去吃。
text.pinyin: A: Nà jiā cāntīng de niúròu miàn zěnmeyàng? B: Tài hǎochī le, wǒ chángcháng qù chī.
text.english: A: How are that restaurant’s beef noodles? B: They are so delicious; I often go eat them.

words.meaning: links a description or owner to a noun
how is it; what do you think
marks a new or strong situation

questions.correctFeedback: The person comes first; 太…了 wraps the description 累.

LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.lessonTitleEnglish: Would You Like Coffee or Tea?
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleTraditional: 第二個人／事物 + 也 + 相同情況
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.titleEnglish: Echo the Same Situation with 也
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.learnerPromise: You can add that another person or thing does the same thing or feels the same way.
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.explanation: First say one situation. In the next part of the sentence, put 也 before the repeated action or description. 也 tells the listener that another person or thing matches what was already said.

teachingGlossary.meaning: marks a new or strong situation
links a description or owner to a noun
how about it; okay or not
ending word that makes a yes-or-no question
how is it; what do you think

LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.pattern: First situation, second person or thing + 也 + same result

discoveryLab.title: Send an echo with 也
discoveryLab.description: The first part of the sentence states a fact. 也 tells the listener that the next person, thing, or action matches it.

choices.label: Same person, another quality
choices.pinyin: Tā hěn piàoliang, yě hěn kě’ài.
choices.english: She is beautiful and also cute.
choices.note: The same person stays; 也 adds another matching description.

choices.label: Same person, another thing
choices.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi shū, yě mǎi bǐ.
choices.english: I buy books and also pens.
choices.note: 買 is repeated after 也 because the second thing shares the same action.

choices.label: Another person
choices.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi shū, tā yě mǎi shū.
choices.english: I buy books; he buys books too.
choices.note: The new person 他 comes before 也.

choices.label: Repair placement
choices.traditional: 也他買書 → 他也買書
choices.simplified: 也他买书 → 他也买书
choices.pinyin: Yě tā mǎi shū → tā yě mǎi shū
choices.note: Name the matching person or thing before 也.

discoveryLab.takeaway: New person or thing first, 也 second, shared result after it.

items.question: Does 也 go before the person?
items.answer: No. Name the matching person first, then 也, then the repeated action: 他也買書.

items.question: Another person does the same thing — do I say the action again?
items.answer: Yes. Repeat the action word after 也. You cannot skip it.

right.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi shū, tā yě mǎi shū.
right.english: I buy books; he buys books too.

items.question: How do I say "I do not like it either"?
items.answer: 也 comes before 不: 我也不喜歡. The order is 也 + 不 + action word.

right.english: I do not like coffee either.

text.traditional: A：你喜歡什麼顏色？ B：我喜歡紅色，也喜歡白色。
text.simplified: A：你喜欢什么颜色？ B：我喜欢红色，也喜欢白色。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xǐhuān shénme yánsè? B: Wǒ xǐhuān hóngsè, yě xǐhuān báisè.
text.english: A: What colors do you like? B: I like red and also white.

text.traditional: A：你們要喝什麼飲料？ B：他要喝奶茶，我也要喝奶茶。
text.simplified: A：你们要喝什么饮料？ B：他要喝奶茶，我也要喝奶茶。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen yào hē shénme yǐnliào? B: Tā yào hē nǎichá, wǒ yě yào hē nǎichá.
text.english: A: What do you want to drink? B: He wants milk tea; I want milk tea too.

text.traditional: A：哪件衣服好看？ B：這件衣服很好看，那件衣服也很好看。
text.simplified: A：哪件衣服好看？ B：这件衣服很好看，那件衣服也很好看。
text.pinyin: A: Nǎ jiàn yīfu hǎokàn? B: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn hǎokàn, nà jiàn yīfu yě hěn hǎokàn.
text.english: A: Which item of clothing looks nice? B: This one looks nice; that one does too.

LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.exercisePreview: Complete each second situation with 也.
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.exerciseInstruction: Say the new person or thing when needed, then put 也 before the repeated result.
LESSON_FOUR_GRAMMAR_TWO.exerciseNote: The source prompts are open. These app models keep the required 也 structure and beginner vocabulary.

segments.traditional: A：你要吃什麼？ B：我想吃牛肉麵，
segments.simplified: A：你要吃什么？ B：我想吃牛肉面，

segments.hint: Add another food with 也 before the repeated action.

questions.correctFeedback: 也 comes before the repeated action 想吃.
questions.repairFeedback: Use 也 + 想吃 + the second food.

segments.traditional: A：那家餐廳什麼好吃？ B：牛肉麵很好吃，
segments.simplified: A：那家餐厅什么好吃？ B：牛肉面很好吃，

segments.hint: Name the second food before 也.

questions.correctFeedback: 蛋糕 is the new matching thing, so it comes before 也.
questions.repairFeedback: Use second thing + 也 + shared description.

segments.traditional: A：誰喜歡買便宜的東西？ B：友美喜歡，
segments.simplified: A：谁喜欢买便宜的东西？ B：友美喜欢，

segments.hint: Add the second person before 也.

questions.correctFeedback: 中明 is the new matching person, so 中明 comes before 也.
questions.repairFeedback: Use person + 也 + shared action.

choices.note: Name the matching person or thing before 也.

discoveryLab.takeaway: New person or thing first, 也 second, shared result after it.

items.question: Does 也 go before the person?
items.answer: No. Name the matching person first, then 也, then the repeated action: 他也買書.

items.question: Another person does the same thing — do I say the action again?
items.answer: Yes. Repeat the action word after 也. You cannot skip it.

right.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi shū, tā yě mǎi shū.
right.english: I buy books; he buys books too.

items.question: How do I say "I do not like it either"?
items.answer: 也 comes before 不: 我也不喜歡. The order is 也 + 不 + action word.

right.english: I do not like coffee either.

text.traditional: A：你喜歡什麼顏色？ B：我喜歡紅色，也喜歡白色。
text.simplified: A：你喜欢什么颜色？ B：我喜欢红色，也喜欢白色。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xǐhuān shénme yánsè? B: Wǒ xǐhuān hóngsè, yě xǐhuān báisè.
text.english: A: What colors do you like? B: I like red and also white.

text.traditional: A：你們要喝什麼飲料？ B：他要喝奶茶，我也要喝奶茶。
text.simplified: A：你们要喝什么饮料？ B：他要喝奶茶，我也要喝奶茶。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐmen yào hē shénme yǐnliào? B: Tā yào hē nǎichá, wǒ yě yào hē nǎichá.
text.english: A: What do you want to drink? B: He wants milk tea; I want milk tea too.

text.traditional: A：哪件衣服好看？ B：這件衣服很好看，那件衣服也很好看。
text.simplified: A：哪件衣服好看？ B：这件衣服很好看，那件衣服也很好看。
text.pinyin: A: Nǎ jiàn yīfu hǎokàn? B: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn hǎokàn, nà jiàn yīfu yě hěn hǎokàn.
text.english: A: Which item of clothing looks nice? B: This one looks nice; that one does too.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Would You Like Coffee or Tea?
grammarPages.learnerPromise: React naturally when something feels extremely hot, big, tiring, good, or delicious.
grammarPages.explanation: Wrap a description with 太 before it and 了 after it. The frame can mean “too,” or an enthusiastic “so” or “really,” depending on context.

discoveryLab.title: Turn up the reaction meter
discoveryLab.description: 太…了 frames one description. Context tells you whether the reaction is delighted or uncomfortable.
discoveryLab.prompt: What kind of reaction do you hear?

choices.label: Delighted
choices.pinyin: Tài hǎo le!
choices.note: With 好, the strong reaction is enthusiastic and positive.

choices.label: Too much
choices.pinyin: Tài dà le!
choices.note: With 大, it can mean "too big" — more than what fits.

choices.label: Very impressed
choices.pinyin: Tài hǎochī le!
choices.note: With 好吃, the speaker reacts with delight.

choices.label: Close the frame
choices.pinyin: tài rè → tài rè le
choices.note: In this pattern, 了 closes the strong reaction.

discoveryLab.takeaway: Open with 太, name the feeling, close with 了.

items.question: Can I just say 太熱?
items.answer: As a full reaction, no — close the frame with 了: 太熱了. 太 and 了 work as a pair.

words.meaning: marks a new or strong situation

items.question: Where does 太 go?
items.answer: Right before the describing word: 太累. The order is 太 + describing word + 了.

words.meaning: marks a new or strong situation

items.question: The shirt is much too big. Is 太好了 okay?
items.answer: No — 太好 sounds happy. Pick the describing word that fits: 太大了.

right.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu tài dà le.
right.english: This item of clothing is too big.
